title: Inside minions: how Stripe uses autonomous one-shot AI coding agents
summary: Stripe engineer demos 'minions', one-shot sandboxed coding agents that turn upfront context into CI-passing pull requests for human review.

assertions.quote: we have at the order of like thousands of PRs now being created by minions

verdicts.note: Background agents do produce usable PRs for well-scoped chores, but merge rates vary widely and many PRs need iteration; 'most of the time' is optimistic.

assertions.quote: we want the agent to be given enough context to accomplish this task in one shot

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: I'm just going to ask an agent first before we kick off the one shot, just to gather some context up front.

verdicts.note: Plan-then-execute consistently reduces agent rework in practice and in vendor evals, especially on multi-file tasks.

assertions.quote: minions are very capable of larger feature changes that are well scoped out by the engineer in advance and then handed off to them

verdicts.note: Current agents are weakest at intent/requirements and strongest at well-specified implementation with verification.

assertions.quote: the minions are, first of all, running in a sandbox developer environment

verdicts.note: Agents have deleted files and run destructive commands when unrestricted; vendors themselves recommend containers/VMs for skip-permissions modes.

assertions.quote: read the code myself to make sure it's a sensible change

verdicts.note: Given documented defect and security rates in AI code, human review before merge is standard practice (e.g. Amazon's two-person rule for AI-assisted changes); it's a sound norm.
